title: Machine identity is read from the kernel hostname (gethostname), which macOS derives from the network when HostName is unset, instead of the configured scutil names; PS1 uses COMPUTERNAME
linked: Mission M3 (S5-Profile) design: profile.json -> config.json single writer + machine resolver
observation: On nobul-mac (2026-10-21): `scutil --get ComputerName` = nobul-mac, `scutil --get LocalHostName` = nobul-mac, `scutil --get HostName` = not set, `sysctl -n kern.hostname` = Mac, node `os.hostname()` = Mac. Every matcher reads the kernel name: node os.hostname() in scripts/aitools (user init ~:990), aitools.ps1 (~:914), build-deploy.sh:218, setup-user-claude.sh:118, profile-check.js:116; `hostname -s` in check-lib.sh:48, aitools-install.sh:126; PS1 uses $env:COMPUTERNAME (setup-user-claude.ps1:132, check-lib.ps1:49, aitools-install.ps1:53). deploy.jsonl/checks.jsonl `host` shows the kernel name flipping Mac <-> nobul-mac (S2-Host RCA). No script calls scutil.
expected: reference/user-repo.md 'Machine matching': config.json machineAlias selects the profile, hostname match is the fallback. No spec defines which hostname source to use; the configured, stable name (macOS ComputerName/LocalHostName via scutil) is the commander-preferred source.
impact: This Mac matched no profile and silently resolved to the first profile ('laptop'), so generated deploy scripts and CLAUDE.md carried another machine's company ('Nobul' instead of 'nobul-tech'). Any macOS machine without HostName set can flip profiles between runs depending on the network.
discoveryContext: Session 360aa8f3-8 (2026-10-21) while reconciling issue #9: dotprofile deploy/ showed 'Company: Nobul'. Investigated by delegate S2-Host (/investigate), report .scratch/session-360aa8f3-8/missions/S2-Host/S2-Host-rca.md; hostname sources re-verified by the Session Commander with scutil, sysctl and node.
suggestedResolution: One machine resolver in aitools-lib (bash + PS1) used by every consumer. macOS: `scutil --get LocalHostName` (or ComputerName); Windows: COMPUTERNAME or registry ComputerName; Linux: /etc/hostname. Better: a stable machine ID (IOPlatformUUID / MachineGuid / /etc/machine-id) stored in profiles.<alias>.machine.id, with hostname as a hint only. Owned by mission M3.
rootCause: Machine identity has no single owner or stable key; it is re-derived in ~7 places from gethostname(), whose value on macOS is network-derived when HostName is unset (S2-Host RCA).

title: `aitools user init` never prompts for or persists machineAlias when no profile hostname matches (Path 1: repo already cloned)
observation: scripts/aitools user init Path 1 (~:983-999) and aitools.ps1 (~:906-925) set machine_alias only on a hostname match and never prompt; the config write adds machineAlias only when non-empty (scripts/aitools ~:1212). The installer only preserves an existing alias (aitools-install.sh Step 5). ~/.aitools/config.json on this Mac has userRepoPath but no machineAlias. Session archive 46ee1c2b (2026-06-17) shows install printing 'No profile matches this machine (hostname: Mac)' and user init printing no alias line.
expected: reference/user-repo.md: 'config.json stores machineAlias on each machine' and 'machineAlias -- selects the profile from profile.json. Set during user init or manually.'
impact: Machines whose hostname drifted or never matched have no alias, so every profile lookup falls to the hostname fallback and then the first profile (#76). The remedy the tooling suggests ('run aitools user init') cannot fix it.
discoveryContext: S2-Host RCA, session 360aa8f3-8 (2026-10-21). Audited: scripts/aitools user init paths 1-3, aitools.ps1, aitools-install.sh Step 5, ~/.aitools/config.json.
suggestedResolution: When no profile matches, user init (and the M3 single config writer) prompts with the existing aliases or 'new', always persists the chosen alias, and logs it; non-interactive runs log_error + write_summary ERROR + ACTION. Bash/PS1 parity.

title: Profile selection silently falls back to the first profile when neither machineAlias nor hostname matches, and the spec endorses the silent fallback
observation: build-deploy.sh:219 and setup-user-claude.sh:118-119 use `profiles[alias] || hostname match || Object.values(p.profiles)[0]`; setup-user-claude.ps1 ~:140-142 the same. Only `Profile interpolation: name=... company=Nobul` is logged at info; nothing records which branch chose the profile. reference/user-repo.md 'Machine matching' documents 'Fallback: hostname match, then first profile'.
expected: .claude/rules/script-standards.md (no silent failures in reusable code; summary coverage rule) -- using another machine's identity is a functional error and must surface as WARN/ERROR with a summary row.
impact: Wrong company/identity is interpolated into ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and into the committed dotprofile deploy/ with exit 0 and no warning; observed for this Mac (laptop/'Nobul' instead of new-mac/'nobul-tech').
discoveryContext: S2-Host RCA, session 360aa8f3-8 (2026-10-21); dotprofile deploy/setup-user-claude.* diff showed 'Company: Nobul'.
suggestedResolution: The M3 resolver returns {alias, via} and logs every selection; no match = log_error + write_summary ERROR + ACTION, never another machine's values. Amend reference/user-repo.md 'Machine matching' (protected) accordingly.

title: Profile-mismatch detection (check_profile / Invoke-ProfileCheck via profile-check.js) is console-only, runs after deploy, recommends a command that cannot fix it, and false-positives when a valid alias is set
observation: scripts/aitools check_profile and aitools.ps1 Invoke-ProfileCheck print `profile: ...` warnings with printf/Write-Host (not logged, not counted) after deploy_configs has already run, and say 'Run aitools user init to fix' (which does not set the alias -- #75). profile-check.js:116 compares only os.hostname(), so it reports NO_MACHINE_MATCH even when config.json machineAlias is valid (S2-Host).
expected: .claude/rules/script-standards.md: logging framework required, no raw echo/Write-Host; warnings counted and in the summary panel.
impact: The only detector of the machine-identity failure is invisible in deploy.log, arrives too late to prevent wrong deploys, and will nag falsely once #75 is fixed.
suggestedResolution: Run the profile check before deploy through the M3 resolver; log via log_warn/LogWarn + write_summary; honor machineAlias in profile-check.js; point the ACTION at the command that actually sets the alias.

title: build-deploy.sh bakes the building machine's per-machine values (profile company/name) into the dotprofile deploy/, which is committed once and shared by all of the user's machines
observation: build-deploy.sh profile interpolation resolves one profile at build time and substitutes {{PROFILE_COMPANY}}/{{PROFILE_NAME}} into deploy/setup-user-claude.* (dotprofile deploy/setup-user-claude.sh contained '- Company: Nobul' after a build on this Mac; the remote copy built elsewhere said 'nobul-tech'). deploy/ lives in the dotprofile repo and is committed (deploy-paths.md 'MDM path').
expected: .claude/rules/deploy-paths.md: dev and MDM paths 'must produce equivalent results'; the dev path resolves the profile per machine at runtime.
impact: The committed MDM deploy/ is correct only for whichever machine built it last; every other machine deploying it gets the wrong identity. Pre-push step 7 then flags drift whenever a different machine rebuilds.
discoveryContext: S2-Host RCA plus the dotprofile deploy/ diff observed during the issue #9 reconciliation, session 360aa8f3-8 (2026-10-21).
suggestedResolution: Stop baking per-machine values: embed all profiles (or none) and resolve at runtime with the same resolver logic inlined via inline_lib_*; or drop machine-varying fields from build-time interpolation. Owned by M3.

title: A known machine-identity defect was parked as 'Uninvestigated' in a plan and a handoff for four months instead of being filed
observation: plans/tooling-resolution-and-artifact-registry.md:129 and .aitools/channel/handoffs/handoff-46ee1c2b-1.md:77 record the 'No profile matches this machine' symptom as uninvestigated (2026-06-17); no incident existed until 2026-10-21 (S2-Host RCA).
expected: .claude/rules/incident-governance.md 'Surfacing duty': deficiencies found in a session are filed; mid-task, leave a `TODO(incident):` marker for /audit to find.
impact: The defect kept producing wrong deploys (#76, #78) across sessions while invisible to /audit and the incident registry.
frameworks: PDCA continuous improvement; the harness surfacing duty
suggestedResolution: Have /handoff and plan templates require that every 'uninvestigated' item is either filed via /incident or carries a TODO(incident): marker; extend /audit to scan plans/ and channel/handoffs/ for 'uninvestigated|not investigated'.

title: Dotprofile hook copies permanently shadow shared/hooks in the dev deploy path (resolve_hook precedence), contradicting the managed-file spec and diverging from the MDM path
observation: setup-user-hooks.sh resolve_hook() (~:73-86) prefers <userRepoPath>/claude/hooks/<name> over shared/hooks/<name>; on [a]dopt it writes the hook to BOTH shared/hooks and the dotprofile (~:160-181). build-deploy.sh embeds only shared/hooks then scripts/ (never the dotprofile). On this Mac the dotprofile held harness-db-sessionstart.sh from before commit 7132dce, so the ~/.aitools/bin relocation fix never deployed (removed 2026-10-21 with commander approval).
expected: reference/managed-file-deployment.md 'Shell Script Deployment Detail': hook adopt targets shared/hooks/ (framework code maintained in the aitools repo). .claude/rules/deploy-paths.md: dev and MDM paths produce equivalent results. Commander decision 2026-10-21: one version per hook, in shared/hooks.
impact: Any adopted hook freezes on that machine: later hook fixes from aitools silently never deploy, and dev and MDM machines run different hook code.
discoveryContext: Session 360aa8f3-8 (2026-10-21), dotprofile reconciliation: diffed dotprofile claude/hooks/* against ~/.claude/hooks and origin shared/hooks.
frameworks: Single source of truth for managed configuration; drift detection
suggestedResolution: Mission M6: hook-lifecycle rule (rollout, deploy, adopt, retire); adopt of a manifest hook writes shared/hooks only; resolve_hook uses shared/hooks for manifest hooks; the dotprofile holds only user-created hooks; warn when a dotprofile copy shadows a manifest hook. Fix bash + PS1 and the spec together.
correctiveAction: 2026-10-21: removed the two dotprofile hook copies (harness-db-sessionstart.sh stale, standing-order-guard.sh identical) and the .bak on nobul-mac.

title: setup-user-hooks reverse-discovery prompt uses bare `read -r choice < /dev/tty`, a call site missed by the #29 EOF fix
observation: scripts/setup-user-hooks.sh reverse discovery (~:228-233) prompts '[a]dopt to dotprofile  [s]kip' with `read -r choice < /dev/tty` and gates on `[ -c /dev/tty ]` rather than tty_interactive; v0.73.3 introduced read_tty_choice for this exact failure (#29).
expected: .claude/rules/interactive-menus.md 'Non-interactive fallback': EOF at the prompt logs a warning and takes the default; prompts use tty_interactive.
impact: With a user-created hook present and stdin at EOF (pty with no input), the deploy dies under set -e with no error line or summary row -- the #29 failure mode.
discoveryContext: Session 360aa8f3-8 (2026-10-21), reading setup-user-hooks.sh while placing the hook-lifecycle mission.
suggestedResolution: Use tty_interactive + read_tty_choice (bash) and Test-InteractiveConsole + Read-ConsoleChoice (PS1); check the PS1 twin; grep scripts/ for remaining bare `read ... < /dev/tty`.

title: standing-order-guard blocks read-only `sed -n '<range>p' <file>` as if it modified files
observation: `sed -n 60,75p scripts/setup-user-hooks.sh` was rejected with 'USO: Dedicated tools --: Use the Edit tool instead of sed to modify files' (session 360aa8f3-8, 2026-10-21); delegate S2-Host reported the same block.
expected: USO 'Dedicated tools for file ops' targets file modification; `sed -n ...p` prints and modifies nothing. .claude/rules/hook-rollout.md: checks enforce only after zero false positives.
impact: Agents lose a read-only command and retry with other tools; low cost but a confirmed false positive in an enforce-mode check.
discoveryContext: Session 360aa8f3-8 (2026-10-21), Session Commander and delegate S2-Host.
suggestedResolution: Exempt `sed -n` without -i/w from the modify check (or reset that check to observe per hook-rollout.md); add a smoke-test case.

title: /delegate did not say that worktree-isolated delegates cannot write to the main checkout's .scratch/, so mission briefs named an unwritable output path
observation: Delegate S3-Nine (worktree isolation) was given an output dir under /Users/new-jose/repos/aitools/.scratch/...; Write returned 'This agent is isolated in the worktree ... Edit the worktree copy of this file instead of the shared-checkout path.' It reported WRITE_BLOCKED and wrote to its scratchpad.
expected: /delegate 'Writing the prompt' step 7: name every output at a path the delegate can write.
impact: Every worktree-isolated delegation with a shared-scratch output hits WRITE_BLOCKED; outputs land in a scratchpad the harvester may not see.
suggestedResolution: Done in PR #51: environment-limits entry 'Worktree isolation confines writes'. Close when #51 merges.
correctiveAction: PR nobul-tech/aitools#51 adds the limit to /delegate.

title: /incident skill points to reference/incidents.json, which moved to registries/incidents.json in v0.69.0
observation: .claude/skills/incident/SKILL.md intent, Step 1 ('Read reference/incidents.json'), Step 5 and Cross-References name reference/incidents.json; the registry is registries/incidents.json (RELEASE_NOTES v0.69.0 'Registries consolidated under registries/'). The skill also self-reports 'outdated and ineffective' in Known Limitations.
expected: RELEASE_NOTES v0.69.0: skills repointed to registries/; .claude/rules/governed-data-access.md: the governing skill holds the registry path.
impact: Agents following the skill literally read a missing file and may conclude there are no incidents or create a stray file; same drift class as #70.
suggestedResolution: Repoint every path in the skill to registries/incidents.json; add a check-pre-commit step that greps skills and hooks for reference/*.json registry paths.

title: check-post-push step 27 `paste -sd ', '` alternates its delimiters, so 3+ missing prerequisites render as 'a,b c'
observation: paste uses ', ' as a delimiter LIST (comma, then space, cycling), not a two-character separator (reported by delegate S3-Nine; the missing '-' operand was fixed in PR #50).
expected: Step 27 message lists missing prerequisites comma-separated.
suggestedResolution: `paste -sd ',' - | perl -pe 's/,/, /g'` or build the list in a loop.

title: A build-deploy.sh failure after its `rm -rf "$DEPLOY_DIR"` leaves the dotprofile deploy/ half-built until the next successful build
observation: build-deploy.sh deletes and recreates DEPLOY_DIR (<userRepoPath>/deploy) before generating scripts; any later exit 1 (e.g. the new embed-loop failure, a sentinel miss) leaves a partially written tree in the dotprofile working copy (reported by S3-Nine).
expected: .claude/rules/config-file-safety.md: a failed write must leave the existing artifact intact (write temp -> validate -> replace).
impact: A failed build destroys the last good MDM deploy/ on that machine; if committed by accident it propagates a broken deploy to every machine.
suggestedResolution: Build into a temp dir beside DEPLOY_DIR, validate (bash -n, PS1 parse, file count), then swap atomically (mv); keep the previous tree on failure and log the path.
